headline: NVDA's Huang probe hits the one AI name desks were hiding in, while the hyperscaler-over-neocloud rotation and the 'flush is late-stage' read both carry into Monday.
market_read: The weekend added a single-name shock to a market already de-grossed: NVDA traded -5% to -6% after Huang admitted the affair and the board opened a probe (Rothschild, GS, Jefferies desks, 9 Nov), even as NVDA topped Barclays' list of names semis investors hide in. Flow data says positioning is much cleaner (GS prime: largest gross-leverage drop since Covid; JPM: biggest multi-strat de-gross since Covid) but not yet at clear capitulation (JPM PI, GS risk appetite, SIG). Pre-market, GS's desk has hyperscalers bid and levered data-center plays (CRWV, IREN, NBIS) sold, the same rotation UBS and Bernstein reported on 7 Nov. On the midterms, UBS's checks and JPM argue Texas risk is mostly a 2028+ new-permit issue rather than halted builds.

up.why: Third straight read of the same rotation: GS's TMT desk (Kamshad, 9 Nov) has hyperscalers bid pre-market (MSFT +2%) while levered DC plays sell; UBS's Dwyer (8 Nov) relays the bull pitch that less capex against a scarcer powered base is a clean FCF-revision story; UBS research (Keirstead, 8 Nov) names MSFT its defensive AI play. SIG (9 Nov) notes MSFT CDS improved last week. Monitor (through 6 Nov): HOT 38.9 (20–<40 band, own h5 median -0.03%, n=4, too thin) and BULL 46.6 (40–<60, h5 median +0.41%, 56.5% up, n=46); no Bloomberg-X move. 1-5 days: the hyperscaler-over-semis rotation can persist while NVDA headlines weigh on AI compute. 2-4 weeks: holds only if 'slower buildout = better FCF' stays the market's reading rather than 'less AI revenue'.
up.confirm: MSFT/AMZN keep outperforming SOX through CRWV/NBIS prints; more desks report long-only buying of hyperscalers.
up.weaken: A broad AI-beta rebound pulls money back into semis, or capex cuts start to be read as weaker demand.

up.why: GS's TMT desk (9 Nov) has AMZN +3% pre-market at the head of the hyperscaler bid; JPM's Dubravko (relayed by Tyler, 9 Nov) argues tighter compute capacity helps hyperscaler pricing power and cash flow. Divergence: SIG (9 Nov) lists AMZN among last week's largest CDS widenings, so the credit side is not cheering. Monitor (through 6 Nov): HOT 40.8 (40–<60, own h5 median -0.36%, 43.9% up, n=41; h10 median +0.67%) and BULL 46.2 (h5 median +0.71%, h10 +2.46%, n=46). 1-5 days: participates in the hyperscaler bid. 2-4 weeks: the CDS divergence makes this lower conviction than MSFT.
up.confirm: AMZN CDS stabilises while the stock holds the pre-market gain; desks cite long-only buying.
up.weaken: AMZN CDS keeps widening or the rotation reverses into AI compute.

up.why: Barclays' desk (Rand, 9 Nov) lists TSMC among the large caps semis investors are hiding in; BofA (Haas Liu, 9 Nov, after 60+ US/EU investor meetings) and UBS (Sunny Lin, 8 Nov) both put TSMC first as the tech leader; Rothschild's desk had TSMC +5% Monday as Taiwan's stabilization fund activated. Divergence: Fubon sales trading (via Jefferies, 9 Nov) doubts the US$15.2B fund can absorb ~US$3.2B/day of foreign selling and flags margin-call deleveraging. No TSM analog or Bloomberg-X data in monitor.json. 1-5 days: watch the T+3 margin-call window (9-13 Nov) and October sales on 10 Nov. 2-4 weeks: the 'quality semis' refuge if forced selling ends.
up.confirm: TAIEX margin-call selling eases this week and TSMC October sales hold up; more desks cite long-only buying of TSM.
up.weaken: Margin calls force another leg of Taiwan selling, or Texas fab news meets political resistance.

up.why: Two desks independently: Barclays (Rand, 9 Nov) says investors still prefer TXN long within analog (long TXN/ADI vs short NXPI/ON) as a stock-picking cycle not purely tied to AI risk-on/off; GS's Callahan (8 Nov) has had several conversations on analog's resilience vs industrials (TXN vs CAT). UBS's Arcuri (9 Nov) calls analog a possible 'safe port'. No TXN analog band or Bloomberg-X move in monitor.json, so this is desk evidence only. 1-5 days: defensive-semis bid while AI compute is headline-driven. 2-4 weeks: fades if the AI bid returns broadly.
up.confirm: TXN outperforms SOX on down days this week; more desks report analog inflows.
up.weaken: Rotation back into high-beta AI semis, or weak industrial data.

down.why: Headline and governance risk, not crowding: Huang admitted an affair with a woman reported to be a suspected Chinese spy and the board opened an independent probe (8 Nov). Desks have NVDA -5% to -6% off-hours/pre-market (Rothschild, GS, Jefferies, 9 Nov); 22V (Hirson) sees more export-control pressure, Stratechery (Thompson, via Grozdea) says his influence will never be the same, Redburn separates a personal scandal from a governance or intelligence compromise. UBS Asia semis (Lin) also flags a slower Rubin ramp in 4Q. Divergent: valuation buyers remain: GS GIR (~11x CY27 EPS), UBS Arcuri (cheapest vs its 10-year history after SITM), Barclays' desk (top long-side hiding name), and SIG saw Feb call spreads bought on Friday, before the news. monitor.json has no NVDA analog band and its Bloomberg-X window ends 6 Nov, before the story. 1-5 days: headline-driven, more reporting can extend the drop. 2-4 weeks: the 17 Nov print and any board/CEO outcome dominate.
down.confirm: Further reporting implicates governance or export compliance; desks report long-only selling rather than HF-only.
down.weaken: Board finds no compromise quickly, Huang stays, and the 17 Nov guide refocuses on fundamentals.

down.why: Neocloud supply continues: GS's TMT desk (9 Nov) has CRWV with IREN and NBIS down 2-5% pre-market while hyperscalers rally, the same rotation UBS and Bernstein flagged on 7 Nov. Reports Tuesday 10 Nov. Monitor (through 6 Nov): HOT 36.8 (20–<40) whose own h5 median is +11.9% but on only n=5, so it is not a reliable offset. 1-5 days: the print is binary given financing focus. 2-4 weeks: depends on financing access, which desks treat as the bear case.
down.confirm: CRWV print shows financing or power-activation slippage; desks keep funding hyperscaler longs with neocloud sales.
down.weaken: A clean print with funded capacity and a broad AI-beta bounce.

down.why: GS's TMT desk (9 Nov) groups NBIS with CRWV/IREN as levered data-center plays under pre-market pressure. BofA research (Liani, via Fenske, 8 Nov) stays constructive but says power activation is the key to converting demand into revenue into Thursday's print. Monitor (through 6 Nov): HOT 25.6 (20–<40, own h5 median -6.1%, n=10) and BULL 33.6 (h5 median +2.8%, n=8), mixed and thin. 1-5 days: trades with CRWV into Tuesday, then its own print Thursday. 2-4 weeks: power activation and financing.
down.confirm: CRWV disappoints on Tuesday and NBIS power activation slips.
down.weaken: Strong activation update and pricing on Thursday.

down.why: Desks are split but the flow skew is negative: Jefferies (Favuzza, 9 Nov) has memory lagging pre-market on the Nikkei report that Terafab targets ~700k wpm of memory by 2032; Barclays (Rand, 9 Nov) says many investors run long HDD / short memory and stay cautious despite low P/Es; GS's Callahan (8 Nov) calls DRAM at 2-3x forward P/E a live debate. Divergent: BofA's Fenske (8 Nov) relays an investor buying DRAM at ~1.5x 2029 P/E, UBS's program desk saw passive buying in memory (Dwyer, 8 Nov), and SIG saw SK Hynix Feb calls bought. monitor.json has no MU analog band; SK Hynix Bloomberg-X attention fell (dz -1.89, 7-day return -20%, through 6 Nov). 1-5 days: Terafab supply headline weighs. 2-4 weeks: valuation buyers vs supply fears, with TrendForce expert calls on 9-10 Nov.
down.confirm: More desks report shorts in memory, or TrendForce flags softer contract pricing.
down.weaken: Spot/contract DRAM prices stay firm and long-only valuation buyers broaden.

down.why: Credit-led: SIG (9 Nov) lists ORCL among last week's largest CDS widenings while MSFT/NVDA/GOOGL/META CDS improved; The Information (9 Nov) repeats the 7 Nov report that MSFT ended its server-rental deal with Oracle (already in the ledger, not a new claim). Divergent: UBS's data-center checks (Keirstead, 8 Nov) quote Oracle saying all five mega-sites are under construction with only NM awaiting a permit. Monitor (through 6 Nov): HOT 57.6 (40–<60, own h5 median +0.41%, n=29) and BULL 43.6 (h5 median +1.37%, n=38), so attention was elevated rather than fading. 1-5 days: tracks AI credit spreads. 2-4 weeks: financing narrative into the December print.
down.confirm: ORCL CDS keeps widening or more hyperscaler rental exits surface.
down.weaken: AI credit spreads tighten and Oracle re-lets the MSFT capacity.

themes.title: Capitulation, or not yet? Desks agree on the flush, disagree on the bottom
themes.text: GS (Armbrust, 9 Nov) reports the largest weekly drop in US fundamental L/S gross leverage since Covid and net leverage at the 0th 5-year percentile; JPM (See, 8 Nov) calls this a positioning unwind near capitulation (biggest multi-strat de-gross since Covid, momentum L/S -40%); Jefferies (Favuzza) counts six weeks and >$20B of HF and LO net selling of tech. Against that, JPM Positioning Intelligence says the TPM buy signal has not triggered, GS's risk-appetite index is not yet at buy levels, and SIG (9 Nov) notes momentum crowding still in the 88th percentile with $60-135bn of possible vol-control selling. UBS's Arcuri (9 Nov) adds that Thursday's drop was macro, systematic and retail AI beta, not HF single-stock unwinds. Weighting: we give the flow data (GS prime, JPM PI) more weight than the narrative, since they are measured; they say 'cleaner, not clean'.

themes.title: Midterms and Texas permits: 2027 protected, 2028 is the debate
themes.text: UBS's Keirstead (8 Nov) ran 15+ data-center checks at DCD Connect: political messaging targets new permits (2028+), not projects mid-build, and the squeeze falls on speculative long-tail projects. JPM (See) says 41% of planned US data-center developments sit in states whose new governor favors a pause, but expects delays or relocation, not denial. BofA (Haas Liu, 9 Nov) models 40 GW of AI compute added in 2027 and 53 GW in 2028 (base), with 45 GW or a flat 40 GW as downside cases (BofA's own GW basis, not facility GW). UBS Taiwan strategy (Chen) sees ~30% of planned 2028 US additions potentially affected; Jefferies' digital-infra analyst cut 2026-30 to 112.8 GW from 122.4 GW. UBS's Dwyer frames the live semis debate as whether the cycle peak is pulled into 2027 or extended.

themes.title: NVDA: the export-control channel matters more than the scandal
themes.text: Redburn (9 Nov) separates a personal affair from a governance failure or an intelligence compromise; 22V (Hirson) argues the bigger investor risk is policy: tighter China export controls (MATCH Act, AI OVERWATCH, remote-access rules) and lost Nvidia influence in Washington ahead of the Trump-Xi meeting on 18-19 Nov. Vital Knowledge recalls Culper's claim that Chinese users could be up to ~20% of compute revenue. Stratechery (Thompson, forwarded by Grozdea) notes Nvidia's role as a financing source for AI infrastructure is also at stake. These are independent and research voices, not desk flows.

themes.title: FundaAI: medium-term demand gap and slower Asian deliveries
themes.text: FundaAI (independent author, 9 Nov weekly) separates horizons: long-term AGI optimism is higher than before, but through 2027 lab revenue leans on VC-funded startups and big tech already optimizing token use, enterprise surveys point to slower adoption, and the Asian supply chain reports slower deliveries and procurement schedules (not yet order cuts). It sees ~0.5-1 GW of on-orbit compute by end-2028 (SPCX). No DAMNANG or SemiAnalysis mail arrived in this window.

source_notes: Channel: Outlook desktop COM (desk_mail_collect.ps1), inbox lag 0 h, no errors; 432 messages screened, 184 bodies retrieved, ~42 read in depth (registered desk senders first, then research and independent sources on the NVDA, midterm and positioning stories).
